h.strategy: Before writing hypotheses, decide which field values typically appear in strong configurations and which in weak ones. A condition that fixes such a value mostly selects strong (or weak) parents. Use this deliberately. Strong parents have little room left, so edits that usually help gain less there, and edits that usually hurt lose more. Weak parents sit near a floor, so harmful edits cost little and helpful edits gain a lot. Write at least six hypotheses where this quality effect predicts the opposite direction to the most obvious story about how the parts connect. Write the remaining ones on the strongest effects you are confident in. Use only conditions that many parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across edited fields and edit values. In each 'why', name the quality mechanism.

hyps.why: A parent with a removed edge is a weak cell near the accuracy floor, so adding a 3x3 conv has much more headroom to gain than in an already strong cell.
A strong parent with a conv3x3 has the most to lose, so removing an edge costs more there than in a weak parent already near the floor.
Skip connections mainly rescue weak cells, so a strong conv3x3 parent has little room left for the gain.
A weak parent is already near the floor, so swapping in a pooling op costs little, while in strong parents it replaces useful capacity.
A strong conv3x3 parent has high accuracy to lose, so a pooling edit hurts more there than in weak parents.
When the direct edge is already none the cell is weak and near the floor, so removing another edge costs little relative to strong parents.
A pooling parent is weak and has headroom, so adding a conv on the other path into the output gains more than in strong parents.
A strong parent with conv3x3 into the output gains little from a skip, and replacing a conv on edge 0 loses relatively more.
A strong parent is near saturation, so an additional conv3x3 has diminishing returns compared with weaker parents.
A parent with edge 4 removed is weak and has fewer paths into the output, so a conv3x3 on the direct edge gains a lot from the headroom.
